stdout_tail:
Both files are in place and valid.

**Finding (H4):** On this dataset (~75%/25% class split), addressing imbalance via `class_weight='balanced'` or SMOTE does **not** improve threshold-independent quality (ROC-AUC stays ~0.89–0.91, PR-AUC actually drops slightly) and it lowers raw accuracy (by 1–4 points). What it does do is shift the operating point: minority-class (`>50K`) recall jumps substantially (+6 to +26 points depending on model/method) at the cost of precision, which raises balanced accuracy (+1.2 to +6.4 points) and minority F1 modestly. So "improvement" is metric-dependent — it helps if you care about balanced/minority-class performance, but hurts on raw accuracy and doesn't move ranking quality (ROC-AUC) at all.

Files written: `analysis.py` and `result.json` in the working directory.

parsed_result.summary: Addressing class imbalance (via class_weight='balanced' or SMOTE) does not improve overall model quality (ROC-AUC/PR-AUC are essentially unchanged, and plain accuracy drops) but it substantially rebalances errors: recall on the minority '>50K' class rises sharply while precision on that class falls, raising balanced accuracy and F1-macro. Whether this counts as an 'improvement' depends on whether the user cares about balanced-class performance or overall/majority-weighted accuracy.
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: mean delta in balanced accuracy (imbalance-handled - baseline), averaged over LogReg class_weight, RF class_weight, RF+SMOTE
parsed_result.direction: imbalance-handling > baseline on balanced accuracy/F1/minority recall; baseline > imbalance-handling on raw accuracy/precision; ROC-AUC ~unchanged
parsed_result.methodological_choices: Dropped rows with missing values (marked '?'); dropped fnlwgt (sampling weight, not a real predictor) and 'education' (redundant with education-num); one-hot encoded categoricals, standard-scaled numerics; 75/25 stratified train/test split, random_state=42. Compared two model families (LogisticRegression, RandomForest with 300 trees) under three imbalance-handling strategies: none (baseline), class_weight='balanced', and SMOTE oversampling (RF only, applied to training data only, after encoding). Evaluated with ROC-AUC, PR-AUC/average precision, balanced accuracy, F1-macro, minority-class F1/recall/precision, and plain accuracy — balanced accuracy was chosen as the primary summary metric since it is directly sensitive to class imbalance handling, unlike ROC-AUC which is threshold-independent and barely moves. Did not tune hyperparameters via CV (fixed reasonable defaults) since the question is about imbalance handling, not model tuning.
